# Himalayan Climbing Expeditions

The data this week comes from [The Himalayan Database](https://www.himalayandatabase.com/).

>The Himalayan Database is a compilation of records for all expeditions that have climbed in the Nepal Himalaya. The database is based on the expedition archives of Elizabeth Hawley, a longtime journalist based in Kathmandu, and it is supplemented by information gathered from books, alpine journals and correspondence with Himalayan climbers.
>
>The data cover all expeditions from 1905 through Spring 2019 to more than 465 significant peaks in Nepal. Also included are expeditions to both sides of border peaks such as Everest, Cho Oyu, Makalu and Kangchenjunga as well as to some smaller border peaks. Data on expeditions to trekking peaks are included for early attempts, first ascents and major accidents.

h/t to [Alex Cookson](https://twitter.com/alexcookson) for sharing and cleaning this data!

This [blog post](https://www.alexcookson.com/post/analyzing-himalayan-peaks-first-ascents/) by [Alex Cookson](https://twitter.com/alexcookson) explores the data in greater detail.

I don't want to underplay that there are some positives and some awful negatives for native Sherpa climbers. [One-third of Everest deaths are Sherpa Climbers](https://www.npr.org/sections/parallels/2018/04/14/599417489/one-third-of-everest-deaths-are-sherpa-climbers).  

Also National Geographic has [5 Ways to help the Sherpas of Everest](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2014/4/140424-sherpas-avalanche-help-donations/).

### Get the data here

```r
# Get the Data

# Read in with tidytuesdayR package 
# Install from CRAN via: install.packages("tidytuesdayR")
# This loads the readme and all the datasets for the week of interest

# Either ISO-8601 date or year/week works!

tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load('2020-09-22')
tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2020, week = 39)

climbers <- tuesdata$climbers

# Or read in the data manually

members <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-09-22/members.csv')
expeditions <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-09-22/expeditions.csv')
peaks <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-09-22/peaks.csv')
```
# Data Dictionary

### `peaks.csv`

| variable                   | class     | description                                                  |
| :------------------------- | :-------- | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
| peak_id                    | character | Unique identifier for peak                                   |
| peak_name                  | character | Common name of peak                                          |
| peak_alternative_name      | character | Alternative name of peak (for example, the "Mount Everest" is "Sagarmatha" in Nepalese) |
| height_metres              | double    | Height of peak in metres                                     |
| climbing_status            | character | Whether the peak has been climbed                            |
| first_ascent_year          | double    | Year of first successful ascent, if applicable               |
| first_ascent_country       | character | Country name(s) of expedition members part of the first ascent. Can have multiple values if members were from different countries. Country name is as of date of ascent (for example, "W Germany" for ascents before 1990). |
| first_ascent_expedition_id | character | Unique identifier for expedition. Can be linked to `expeditions` or `members` tables. |



### `expeditions.csv`

| variable           | class     | description                                                  |
| :----------------- | :-------- | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
| expedition_id      | character | Unique identifier for expedition. Can be linked to `peaks` or `members` tables. |
| peak_id            | character | Unique identifier for peak. Can be linked to `peaks` table.  |
| peak_name          | character | Common name for peak                                         |
| year               | double    | Year of expedition                                           |
| season             | character | Season of expedition (Spring, Summer, etc.)                  |
| basecamp_date      | date      | Date of expedition arrival at basecamp                       |
| highpoint_date        | date      | Date of expedition summiting the peak for the first time or, if peak wasn't reached, date of reaching its highpoint |
| termination_date   | date      | Date the expedition was terminated                           |
| termination_reason | character | Primary reason the expedition was terminated. There are two possibilities for a successful expeditions, depending on whether the main peak or a sub-peak was summitted. |
| highpoint_metres   | double    | Elevation highpoint of the expedition                        |
| members            | double    | Number of expedition members. For expeditions in Nepal, this is usually the number of foreigners listed on the expedition permit. For expeditions in China, this is usually the number of non-hired members. |
| member_deaths      | double    | Number of expeditions members who died                       |
| hired_staff        | double    | Number of hired staff who went above basecamp                |
| hired_staff_deaths | double    | Number of hired staff who died                               |
| oxygen_used        | logical   | Whether oxygen was used by at least one member of the expedition |
| trekking_agency    | character | Name of the trekking agency                                  |



### `members.csv`

| variable             | class     | description                                                  |
| :------------------- | :-------- | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
| expedition_id        | character | Unique identifier for expedition. Can be linked to `peaks` or `members` tables. |
| member_id            | character | Unique identifier for the person. This is *not* consistent across expeditions, so you cannot use a single `member_id` to look up all expeditions a person was part of. |
| peak_id              | character | Unique identifier for peak. Can be linked to `peaks` table.  |
| peak_name            | character | Common name for peak                                         |
| year                 | double    | Year of expedition                                           |
| season               | character | Season of expedition (Spring, Summer, etc.)                  |
| sex                  | character | Sex of the person                                            |
| age                  | double    | Age of the person. Depending on the best available data, this could be as of the summit date, the date of death, or the date of arrival at basecamp. |
| citizenship          | character | Citizenship of the person                                    |
| expedition_role      | character | Role of the person on the expedition                         |
| hired                | logical   | Whether the person was hired by the expedition               |
| highpoint_metres     | double    | Elevation highpoint of the person                            |
| success              | logical   | Whether the person was successful in summitting a main peak or sub-peak, depending on the goal of expedition |
| solo                 | logical   | Whether the person attempted a solo ascent                   |
| oxygen_used          | logical   | Whether the person used oxygen                               |
| died                 | logical   | Whether the person died                                      |
| death_cause          | character | Primary cause of death                                       |
| death_height_metres  | double    | Height at which the person died                              |
| injured              | logical   | Whether the person was injured                               |
| injury_type          | character | Primary cause of injury                                      |
| injury_height_metres | double    | Height at which the injury occurred                          |


### Cleaning Script

```r
# Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)


# Peaks
peaks <- read_csv("./himalayan-expeditions/raw/peaks.csv") %>%
  transmute(
    peak_id = PEAKID,
    peak_name = PKNAME,
    peak_alternative_name = PKNAME2,
    height_metres = HEIGHTM,
    climbing_status = PSTATUS,
    first_ascent_year = PYEAR,
    first_ascent_country = PCOUNTRY,
    first_ascent_expedition_id = PEXPID
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    climbing_status = case_when(
      climbing_status == 0 ~ "Unknown",
      climbing_status == 1 ~ "Unclimbed",
      climbing_status == 2 ~ "Climbed"
    )
  )

# Create small dataframe of peak names to join to other dataframes
peak_names <- peaks %>%
  select(peak_id, peak_name)

# Expeditions
expeditions <- read_csv("./himalayan-expeditions/raw/exped.csv") %>%
  left_join(peak_names, by = c("PEAKID" = "peak_id")) %>%
  transmute(
    expedition_id = EXPID,
    peak_id = PEAKID,
    peak_name,
    year = YEAR,
    season = SEASON,
    basecamp_date = BCDATE,
    highpoint_date = SMTDATE,
    termination_date = TERMDATE,
    termination_reason = TERMREASON,
    # Highpoint of 0 is most likely missing value
    highpoint_metres = ifelse(HIGHPOINT == 0, NA, HIGHPOINT),
    members = TOTMEMBERS,
    member_deaths = MDEATHS,
    hired_staff = TOTHIRED,
    hired_staff_deaths = HDEATHS,
    oxygen_used = O2USED,
    trekking_agency = AGENCY
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    termination_reason = case_when(
      termination_reason == 0 ~ "Unknown",
      termination_reason == 1 ~ "Success (main peak)",
      termination_reason == 2 ~ "Success (subpeak)",
      termination_reason == 3 ~ "Success (claimed)",
      termination_reason == 4 ~ "Bad weather (storms, high winds)",
      termination_reason == 5 ~ "Bad conditions (deep snow, avalanching, falling ice, or rock)",
      termination_reason == 6 ~ "Accident (death or serious injury)",
      termination_reason == 7 ~ "Illness, AMS, exhaustion, or frostbite",
      termination_reason == 8 ~ "Lack (or loss) of supplies or equipment",
      termination_reason == 9 ~ "Lack of time",
      termination_reason == 10 ~ "Route technically too difficult, lack of experience, strength, or motivation",
      termination_reason == 11 ~ "Did not reach base camp",
      termination_reason == 12 ~ "Did not attempt climb",
      termination_reason == 13 ~ "Attempt rumoured",
      termination_reason == 14 ~ "Other"
    ),
    season = case_when(
      season == 0 ~ "Unknown",
      season == 1 ~ "Spring",
      season == 2 ~ "Summer",
      season == 3 ~ "Autumn",
      season == 4 ~ "Winter"
    )
  )

members <-
  read_csv("./himalayan-expeditions/raw/members.csv", guess_max = 100000) %>%
  left_join(peak_names, by = c("PEAKID" = "peak_id")) %>%
  transmute(
    expedition_id = EXPID,
    member_id = paste(EXPID, MEMBID, sep = "-"),
    peak_id = PEAKID,
    peak_name,
    year = MYEAR,
    season = MSEASON,
    sex = SEX,
    age = CALCAGE,
    citizenship = CITIZEN,
    expedition_role = STATUS,
    hired = HIRED,
    # Highpoint of 0 is most likely missing value
    highpoint_metres = ifelse(MPERHIGHPT == 0, NA, MPERHIGHPT),
    success = MSUCCESS,
    solo = MSOLO,
    oxygen_used = MO2USED,
    died = DEATH,
    death_cause = DEATHTYPE,
    # Height of 0 is most likely missing value
    death_height_metres = ifelse(DEATHHGTM == 0, NA, DEATHHGTM),
    injured = INJURY,
    injury_type = INJURYTYPE,
    # Height of 0 is most likely missing value
    injury_height_metres = ifelse(INJURYHGTM == 0, NA, INJURYHGTM)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    season = case_when(
      season == 0 ~ "Unknown",
      season == 1 ~ "Spring",
      season == 2 ~ "Summer",
      season == 3 ~ "Autumn",
      season == 4 ~ "Winter"
    ),
    age = ifelse(age == 0, NA, age),
    death_cause = case_when(
      death_cause == 0 ~ "Unspecified",
      death_cause == 1 ~ "AMS",
      death_cause == 2 ~ "Exhaustion",
      death_cause == 3 ~ "Exposure / frostbite",
      death_cause == 4 ~ "Fall",
      death_cause == 5 ~ "Crevasse",
      death_cause == 6 ~ "Icefall collapse",
      death_cause == 7 ~ "Avalanche",
      death_cause == 8 ~ "Falling rock / ice",
      death_cause == 9 ~ "Disappearance (unexplained)",
      death_cause == 10 ~ "Illness (non-AMS)",
      death_cause == 11 ~ "Other",
      death_cause == 12 ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    injury_type = case_when(
      injury_type == 0 ~ "Unspecified",
      injury_type == 1 ~ "AMS",
      injury_type == 2 ~ "Exhaustion",
      injury_type == 3 ~ "Exposure / frostbite",
      injury_type == 4 ~ "Fall",
      injury_type == 5 ~ "Crevasse",
      injury_type == 6 ~ "Icefall collapse",
      injury_type == 7 ~ "Avalanche",
      injury_type == 8 ~ "Falling rock / ice",
      injury_type == 9 ~ "Disappearance (unexplained)",
      injury_type == 10 ~ "Illness (non-AMS)",
      injury_type == 11 ~ "Other",
      injury_type == 12 ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    death_cause = ifelse(died, death_cause, NA_character_),
    death_height_metres = ifelse(died, death_height_metres, NA),
    injury_type = ifelse(injured, injury_type, NA_character_),
    injury_height_metres = ifelse(injured, injury_height_metres, NA)
  )


### Write to CSV
write_csv(expeditions, "./himalayan-expeditions/expeditions.csv")
write_csv(members, "./himalayan-expeditions/members.csv")
write_csv(peaks, "./himalayan-expeditions/peaks.csv")

```

pre-commercial (1921-1989) vs commercial (1990-2019) comparison.

Run:  python -I analysis.py   (from this folder; reads ../../data, read-only)
"""
import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "data")
COMMERCIAL_START = 1990

# ---------- load ----------
exp_all = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, "expeditions.csv"))
mem_all = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, "members.csv"), low_memory=False)
exp = exp_all[exp_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()
mem = mem_all[mem_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()
print(f"Everest expeditions: {len(exp)} ({exp.year.min()}-{exp.year.max()})")
print(f"Everest member rows: {len(mem)}")

# Expedition-level totals are the complete record of people and deaths.
# Member-level rows are used for roles, causes and summit detail.
exp["era"] = np.where(exp.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, "Commercial (1990-2019)", "Pre-commercial (1921-1989)")
mem["era"] = np.where(mem.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, "Commercial (1990-2019)", "Pre-commercial (1921-1989)")
exp["decade"] = (exp.year // 10) * 10
mem["decade"] = (mem.year // 10) * 10


def wilson(k, n, z=1.96):
    """Wilson 95% CI for a proportion k/n."""
    if n == 0:
        return (np.nan, np.nan)
    p = k / n
    denom = 1 + z**2 / n
    centre = (p + z**2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = z * np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z**2 / (4 * n**2)) / denom
    return (centre - half, centre + half)


# ---------- 1. decade table (expedition-level totals) ----------
g = exp.groupby("decade")
dec = pd.DataFrame({
    "expeditions": g.size(),
    "members": g.members.sum(),
    "member_deaths": g.member_deaths.sum(),
    "hired_staff": g.hired_staff.sum(),
    "hired_staff_deaths": g.hired_staff_deaths.sum(),
})
dec["member_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.member_deaths / dec.members
dec["hired_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.hired_staff_deaths / dec.hired_staff
dec["hired_per_member"] = dec.hired_staff / dec.members
dec["small_sample_flag"] = (dec.members < 100) | (dec.hired_staff < 100)
dec = dec.reset_index()
dec.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "decade_death_rates.csv"), index=False)
print("\nDecade table:\n", dec.round(2).to_string(index=False))

# ---------- 2. era comparison with CIs and tests ----------
era_rows = []
for era, sub in exp.groupby("era"):
    for who, k_col, n_col in [("Expedition members", "member_deaths", "members"),
                              ("Hired staff", "hired_staff_deaths", "hired_staff")]:
        k, n = int(sub[k_col].sum()), int(sub[n_col].sum())
        lo, hi = wilson(k, n)
        era_rows.append({"era": era, "group": who, "deaths": k, "people": n,
                         "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n, "ci_low_pct": 100 * lo, "ci_high_pct": 100 * hi})
era = pd.DataFrame(era_rows)
era.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_death_rates.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra table:\n", era.round(3).to_string(index=False))

tests = []
pre = exp[exp.era.str.startswith("Pre")]
com = exp[exp.era.str.startswith("Com")]
for who, k_col, n_col in [("Expedition members", "member_deaths", "members"),
                          ("Hired staff", "hired_staff_deaths", "hired_staff")]:
    table = np.array([
        [pre[k_col].sum(), pre[n_col].sum() - pre[k_col].sum()],
        [com[k_col].sum(), com[n_col].sum() - com[k_col].sum()],
    ])
    chi2, p, _, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(table, correction=False)
    rr = (com[k_col].sum() / com[n_col].sum()) / (pre[k_col].sum() / pre[n_col].sum())
    tests.append({"group": who, "rate_ratio_commercial_vs_pre": rr, "chi2": chi2, "p_value": p})
tests = pd.DataFrame(tests)
tests.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_tests.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra tests (person-level chi-square; ignores expedition clustering):\n", tests.to_string(index=False))

# ---------- 3. sensitivity: commercial era without the two icefall/avalanche disasters ----------
# 2014 (Khumbu icefall, 16 Sherpa killed) and 2015 (base camp avalanche, 19 killed)
sens_rows = []
for label, sub in [("Commercial, all years", com),
                   ("Commercial, excl. 2014-2015", com[~com.year.isin([2014, 2015])])]:
    k, n = int(sub.hired_staff_deaths.sum()), int(sub.hired_staff.sum())
    sens_rows.append({"sample": label, "group": "Hired staff", "deaths": k, "people": n, "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n})
    k, n = int(sub.member_deaths.sum()), int(sub.members.sum())
    sens_rows.append({"sample": label, "group": "Expedition members", "deaths": k, "people": n, "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n})
sens = pd.DataFrame(sens_rows)
sens.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "sensitivity_excl_2014_2015.csv"), index=False)
print("\nSensitivity:\n", sens.round(3).to_string(index=False))

# Single-year spikes in hired-staff deaths
yr = exp.groupby("year").agg(hired_staff_deaths=("hired_staff_deaths", "sum"),
                             member_deaths=("member_deaths", "sum"),
                             hired_staff=("hired_staff", "sum"),
                             members=("members", "sum"))
top_years = yr.sort_values("hired_staff_deaths", ascending=False).head(8)
top_years.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "top_years_hired_deaths.csv"))
print("\nTop years by hired-staff deaths:\n", top_years.to_string())

# ---------- 4. commercial-era changes (member-level detail) ----------
mem_m = mem[~mem.hired]  # expedition members (not hired)

for era_name, sub in mem_m.groupby("era"):

print("\nMember profile by era:\n", change.round(2).to_string(index=False))

# Death causes among all Everest deaths in member table, by era
deaths_mem = mem[mem.died]
causes = pd.crosstab(deaths_mem.death_cause, deaths_mem.era)
causes.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "death_causes_by_era.csv"))

# Hired staff per expedition-member (commercial structure)
per_exp = exp.groupby("era").agg(
    expeditions=("expedition_id", "size"),
    mean_members=("members", "mean"),
    mean_hired=("hired_staff", "mean"),
    oxygen_expedition_share_pct=("oxygen_used", lambda s: 100 * s.mean()),
    agency_named_share_pct=("trekking_agency", lambda s: 100 * s.notna().mean()),
)
per_exp.round(2).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_expedition_profile.csv"))
print("\nExpedition profile by era:\n", per_exp.round(2).to_string())

# ---------- 5. charts ----------
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 11, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
C_MEM, C_HIRED, C_GREY = "#1f4e79", "#c0504d", "#7f7f7f"

# Chart 1: death rates by decade

mem = mem_all[mem_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()

print(f"Everest member rows: {len(mem)}")

# Member-level rows are used for roles, causes and summit detail.
exp["era"] = np.where(exp.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, COM, PRE)
mem["era"] = np.where(mem.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, COM, PRE)
exp["decade"] = (exp.year // 10) * 10
mem["decade"] = (mem.year // 10) * 10


def wilson(k, n, z=1.96):
    """Wilson 95% CI for a proportion k/n."""
    if n == 0:
        return (np.nan, np.nan)
    p = k / n
    denom = 1 + z ** 2 / n
    centre = (p + z ** 2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = z * np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z ** 2 / (4 * n ** 2)) / denom
    return (centre - half, centre + half)

    "hired_staff": g.hired_staff.sum(),
    "hired_staff_deaths": g.hired_staff_deaths.sum(),
})

dec["hired_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.hired_staff_deaths / dec.hired_staff
dec["hired_per_member"] = dec.hired_staff / dec.members
dec["small_sample_flag"] = (dec.members < 100) | (dec.hired_staff < 100)

        k, n = int(sub[k_col].sum()), int(sub[n_col].sum())
        lo, hi = wilson(k, n)
        era_rows.append({"era": era_name, "group": who, "deaths": k, "people": n,
                         "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n, "ci_low_pct": 100 * lo, "ci_high_pct": 100 * hi})

print("\nEra table:\n", era.round(3).to_string(index=False))

tests = []

    ])
    chi2, p, _, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(table, correction=False)
    rr = (com[k_col].sum() / com[n_col].sum()) / (pre[k_col].sum() / pre[n_col].sum())
    tests.append({"group": who, "rate_ratio_commercial_vs_pre": rr, "chi2": chi2, "p_value": p})
tests = pd.DataFrame(tests)
tests.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_tests.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra tests (person-level chi-square; ignores expedition clustering):\n", tests.to_string(index=False))

                             member_deaths=("member_deaths", "sum"),
                             hired_staff=("hired_staff", "sum"),

mem_m = mem[~mem.hired].copy()  # expedition members (not hired)

"""Has climbing Mount Everest become safer over time?

Death rates for expedition members vs hired staff, by decade, and the
pre-commercial (1921-1989) vs commercial (1990-2019) comparison.

Run:  python -I analysis.py   (from this folder; reads ../../data, read-only)
"""
import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "data")
COMMERCIAL_START = 1990
PRE = "Pre-commercial (1921-1989)"
COM = "Commercial (1990-2019)"

# ---------- load ----------
exp_all = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, "expeditions.csv"))
mem_all = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, "members.csv"), low_memory=False)
exp = exp_all[exp_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()
mem = mem_all[mem_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()
print(f"Everest expeditions: {len(exp)} ({exp.year.min()}-{exp.year.max()})")
print(f"Everest member rows: {len(mem)}")

# Expedition-level totals are the complete record of people and deaths.
# Member-level rows are used for roles, causes and summit detail.
exp["era"] = np.where(exp.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, COM, PRE)
mem["era"] = np.where(mem.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, COM, PRE)
exp["decade"] = (exp.year // 10) * 10
mem["decade"] = (mem.year // 10) * 10


def wilson(k, n, z=1.96):
    """Wilson 95% CI for a proportion k/n."""
    if n == 0:
        return (np.nan, np.nan)
    p = k / n
    denom = 1 + z ** 2 / n
    centre = (p + z ** 2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = z * np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z ** 2 / (4 * n ** 2)) / denom
    return (centre - half, centre + half)


# ---------- 1. decade table (expedition-level totals) ----------
g = exp.groupby("decade")
dec = pd.DataFrame({
    "expeditions": g.size(),
    "members": g.members.sum(),
    "member_deaths": g.member_deaths.sum(),
    "hired_staff": g.hired_staff.sum(),
    "hired_staff_deaths": g.hired_staff_deaths.sum(),
})
dec["member_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.member_deaths / dec.members
dec["hired_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.hired_staff_deaths / dec.hired_staff
dec["hired_per_member"] = dec.hired_staff / dec.members
dec["small_sample_flag"] = (dec.members < 100) | (dec.hired_staff < 100)
dec = dec.reset_index()
dec.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "decade_death_rates.csv"), index=False)
print("\nDecade table:\n", dec.round(2).to_string(index=False))

# ---------- 2. era comparison with CIs and tests ----------
era_rows = []
for era_name, sub in exp.groupby("era"):
    for who, k_col, n_col in [("Expedition members", "member_deaths", "members"),
                              ("Hired staff", "hired_staff_deaths", "hired_staff")]:
        k, n = int(sub[k_col].sum()), int(sub[n_col].sum())
        lo, hi = wilson(k, n)
        era_rows.append({"era": era_name, "group": who, "deaths": k, "people": n,
                         "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n, "ci_low_pct": 100 * lo, "ci_high_pct": 100 * hi})
era = pd.DataFrame(era_rows)
era.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_death_rates.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra table:\n", era.round(3).to_string(index=False))

pre = exp[exp.era == PRE]
com = exp[exp.era == COM]
tests = []
for who, k_col, n_col in [("Expedition members", "member_deaths", "members"),
                          ("Hired staff", "hired_staff_deaths", "hired_staff")]:
    table = np.array([
        [pre[k_col].sum(), pre[n_col].sum() - pre[k_col].sum()],
        [com[k_col].sum(), com[n_col].sum() - com[k_col].sum()],
    ])
    chi2, p, _, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(table, correction=False)
    rr = (com[k_col].sum() / com[n_col].sum()) / (pre[k_col].sum() / pre[n_col].sum())
    tests.append({"group": who, "rate_ratio_commercial_vs_pre": rr, "chi2": chi2, "p_value": p})
tests = pd.DataFrame(tests)
tests.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_tests.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra tests (person-level chi-square; ignores expedition clustering):\n", tests.to_string(index=False))

# ---------- 3. sensitivity: commercial era without the 2014 and 2015 disasters ----------
# 2014 (Khumbu icefall) and 2015 (base camp avalanche) are the two worst years for hired-staff
# deaths in this data (see top_years_hired_deaths.csv). Event names are outside context, not from data.
sens_rows = []
for label, sub in [("Commercial, all years", com),
                   ("Commercial, excl. 2014-2015", com[~com.year.isin([2014, 2015])])]:
    k, n = int(sub.hired_staff_deaths.sum()), int(sub.hired_staff.sum())
    sens_rows.append({"sample": label, "group": "Hired staff", "deaths": k, "people": n, "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n})
    k, n = int(sub.member_deaths.sum()), int(sub.members.sum())
    sens_rows.append({"sample": label, "group": "Expedition members", "deaths": k, "people": n, "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n})
sens = pd.DataFrame(sens_rows)
sens.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "sensitivity_excl_2014_2015.csv"), index=False)
print("\nSensitivity:\n", sens.round(3).to_string(index=False))

# Single-year spikes in deaths
yr = exp.groupby("year").agg(hired_staff_deaths=("hired_staff_deaths", "sum"),
                             member_deaths=("member_deaths", "sum"),
                             hired_staff=("hired_staff", "sum"),
                             members=("members", "sum"))
top_years = yr.sort_values("hired_staff_deaths", ascending=False).head(8)
top_years.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "top_years_hired_deaths.csv"))
print("\nTop years by hired-staff deaths:\n", top_years.to_string())

# ---------- 4. commercial-era changes (member-level detail) ----------
mem_m = mem[~mem.hired].copy()  # expedition members (not hired)
mem_m["summit"] = mem_m.success.astype(bool)
change = []
for era_name, sub in mem_m.groupby("era"):
    change.append({
        "era": era_name,
        "member_rows": len(sub),
        "oxygen_share_pct": 100 * sub.oxygen_used.mean(),
        "summit_share_pct": 100 * sub.summit.mean(),
        "deaths_per_100_summits": 100 * sub.died.sum() / max(sub.summit.sum(), 1),
        "median_age": sub.age.median(),
        "female_share_pct": 100 * (sub.sex == "F").mean(),
    })
change = pd.DataFrame(change)
change.round(2).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_member_profile.csv"), index=False)
print("\nMember profile by era:\n", change.round(2).to_string(index=False))

# Death causes among Everest deaths in the member table, by era
deaths_mem = mem[mem.died]
causes = pd.crosstab(deaths_mem.death_cause, deaths_mem.era)
causes.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "death_causes_by_era.csv"))
print("\nDeath causes by era (member table):\n", causes.to_string())

# Expedition structure by era
per_exp = exp.groupby("era").agg(
    expeditions=("expedition_id", "size"),
    mean_members=("members", "mean"),
    mean_hired=("hired_staff", "mean"),
    oxygen_expedition_share_pct=("oxygen_used", lambda s: 100 * s.mean()),
    agency_named_share_pct=("trekking_agency", lambda s: 100 * s.notna().mean()),
)
per_exp.round(2).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_expedition_profile.csv"))
print("\nExpedition profile by era:\n", per_exp.round(2).to_string())

# ---------- 5. charts ----------
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 11, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
C_MEM, C_HIRED, C_GREY = "#1f4e79", "#c0504d", "#7f7f7f"

# Chart 1: death rates by decade (1950s onward)
d = dec[dec.decade >= 1950].copy()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ax.plot(d.decade, d.hired_death_rate_pct, marker="o", color=C_HIRED, lw=2.2, label="Hired staff")
ax.plot(d.decade, d.member_death_rate_pct, marker="o", color=C_MEM, lw=2.2, label="Expedition members")
ax.axvline(COMMERCIAL_START, color=C_GREY, ls="--", lw=1)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(d.hired_death_rate_pct.max(), d.member_death_rate_pct.max()) * 1.25)
ax.text(COMMERCIAL_START + 1, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.93, "Commercial era begins (1990)", color=C_GREY, fontsize=10)
ax.set_xlabel("Decade of expedition")
ax.set_ylabel("Deaths per 100 people on expeditions")
ax.set_title("Everest death rates by decade: hired staff vs expedition members")
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right")
for x, y in zip(d.decade, d.hired_death_rate_pct):
    if np.isfinite(y):
        ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 7), ha="center", fontsize=9, color=C_HIRED)
for x, y in zip(d.decade, d.member_death_rate_pct):
    if np.isfinite(y):
        ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, -15), ha="center", fontsize=9, color=C_MEM)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(HERE, "chart1_death_rate_by_decade.png"), dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 2: era comparison with 95% CIs
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
labels = ["Pre-commercial\n(1921-1989)", "Commercial\n(1990-2019)"]
x = np.arange(2)
w = 0.35
for i, (who, col) in enumerate([("Expedition members", C_MEM), ("Hired staff", C_HIRED)]):
    sub = era[era.group == who].set_index("era").loc[[PRE, COM]]
    yerr = [sub.death_rate_pct - sub.ci_low_pct, sub.ci_high_pct - sub.death_rate_pct]
    ax.bar(x + (i - 0.5) * w, sub.death_rate_pct, w, color=col, label=who, yerr=yerr, capsize=4)
    for xi, v in zip(x + (i - 0.5) * w, sub.death_rate_pct):
        ax.text(xi, v + 0.25, f"{v:.1f}%", ha="center", fontsize=10)
ax.set_xticks(x, labels)

ax.set_title("Death rate on Everest, before vs during the commercial era")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(HERE, "chart2_era_comparison.png"), dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 3: people on expeditions per decade
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
d2 = dec[dec.decade >= 1950]
ax.bar(d2.decade, d2.members, width=7, color=C_MEM, alpha=0.85, label="Expedition members")
ax.bar(d2.decade, d2.hired_staff, width=3, color=C_HIRED, alpha=0.9, label="Hired staff (above base camp)")
ax.set_xlabel("Decade of expedition")
ax.set_ylabel("People on Everest expeditions (total)")
ax.set_title("Everest: people on expeditions per decade")
ax.legend(frameon=False)

pre-commercial (1921-1989) vs commercial (1990-2019) comparison.

Run:  python -I analysis.py   (from this folder; reads ../../data, read-only)

import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "data")
COMMERCIAL_START = 1990
PRE = "Pre-commercial (1921-1989)"
COM = "Commercial (1990-2019)"

exp_all = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, "expeditions.csv"))
mem_all = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, "members.csv"), low_memory=False)
exp = exp_all[exp_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()
mem = mem_all[mem_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()
print(f"Everest expeditions: {len(exp)} ({exp.year.min()}-{exp.year.max()})")
print(f"Everest member rows: {len(mem)}")

# Expedition-level totals are the complete record of people and deaths.
# Member-level rows are used for roles, causes and summit detail.
exp["era"] = np.where(exp.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, COM, PRE)
mem["era"] = np.where(mem.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, COM, PRE)
exp["decade"] = (exp.year // 10) * 10
mem["decade"] = (mem.year // 10) * 10


def wilson(k, n, z=1.96):
    """Wilson 95% CI for a proportion k/n."""
    if n == 0:
        return (np.nan, np.nan)
    p = k / n
    denom = 1 + z ** 2 / n
    centre = (p + z ** 2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = z * np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z ** 2 / (4 * n ** 2)) / denom
    return (centre - half, centre + half)


# ---------- 1. decade table (expedition-level totals) ----------
g = exp.groupby("decade")
dec = pd.DataFrame({
    "expeditions": g.size(),
    "members": g.members.sum(),
    "member_deaths": g.member_deaths.sum(),
    "hired_staff": g.hired_staff.sum(),
    "hired_staff_deaths": g.hired_staff_deaths.sum(),
})
dec["member_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.member_deaths / dec.members
dec["hired_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.hired_staff_deaths / dec.hired_staff
dec["hired_per_member"] = dec.hired_staff / dec.members
dec["small_sample_flag"] = (dec.members < 100) | (dec.hired_staff < 100)
dec = dec.reset_index()
dec.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "decade_death_rates.csv"), index=False)
print("\nDecade table:\n", dec.round(2).to_string(index=False))

# ---------- 2. era comparison with CIs and tests ----------
era_rows = []
for era_name, sub in exp.groupby("era"):
    for who, k_col, n_col in [("Expedition members", "member_deaths", "members"),
                              ("Hired staff", "hired_staff_deaths", "hired_staff")]:
        k, n = int(sub[k_col].sum()), int(sub[n_col].sum())
        lo, hi = wilson(k, n)
        era_rows.append({"era": era_name, "group": who, "deaths": k, "people": n,
                         "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n, "ci_low_pct": 100 * lo, "ci_high_pct": 100 * hi})
era = pd.DataFrame(era_rows)
era.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_death_rates.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra table:\n", era.round(3).to_string(index=False))

pre = exp[exp.era == PRE]
com = exp[exp.era == COM]
tests = []
for who, k_col, n_col in [("Expedition members", "member_deaths", "members"),
                          ("Hired staff", "hired_staff_deaths", "hired_staff")]:
    table = np.array([
        [pre[k_col].sum(), pre[n_col].sum() - pre[k_col].sum()],
        [com[k_col].sum(), com[n_col].sum() - com[k_col].sum()],
    ])
    chi2, p, _, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(table, correction=False)
    rr = (com[k_col].sum() / com[n_col].sum()) / (pre[k_col].sum() / pre[n_col].sum())
    tests.append({"group": who, "rate_ratio_commercial_vs_pre": rr, "chi2": chi2, "p_value": p})
tests = pd.DataFrame(tests)
tests.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_tests.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra tests (person-level chi-square; ignores expedition clustering):\n", tests.to_string(index=False))

# ---------- 3. sensitivity: commercial era without the 2014 and 2015 disasters ----------
# 2014 (Khumbu icefall) and 2015 (base camp avalanche) are the two worst years for hired-staff
# deaths in this data (see top_years_hired_deaths.csv). Event names are outside context, not from data.
sens_rows = []
for label, sub in [("Commercial, all years", com),
                   ("Commercial, excl. 2014-2015", com[~com.year.isin([2014, 2015])])]:
    k, n = int(sub.hired_staff_deaths.sum()), int(sub.hired_staff.sum())
    sens_rows.append({"sample": label, "group": "Hired staff", "deaths": k, "people": n, "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n})
    k, n = int(sub.member_deaths.sum()), int(sub.members.sum())
    sens_rows.append({"sample": label, "group": "Expedition members", "deaths": k, "people": n, "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n})

sens.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "sensitivity_excl_2014_2015.csv"), index=False)
print("\nSensitivity:\n", sens.round(3).to_string(index=False))

# Single-year spikes in deaths

                             member_deaths=("member_deaths", "sum"),
                             hired_staff=("hired_staff", "sum"),
                             members=("members", "sum"))
top_years = yr.sort_values("hired_staff_deaths", ascending=False).head(8)
top_years.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "top_years_hired_deaths.csv"))
print("\nTop years by hired-staff deaths:\n", top_years.to_string())

mem_m = mem[~mem.hired].copy()  # expedition members (not hired)

    change.append({
        "era": era_name,
        "member_rows": len(sub),
        "oxygen_share_pct": 100 * sub.oxygen_used.mean(),
        "summit_share_pct": 100 * sub.summit.mean(),
        "deaths_per_100_summits": 100 * sub.died.sum() / max(sub.summit.sum(), 1),
        "median_age": sub.age.median(),
        "female_share_pct": 100 * (sub.sex == "F").mean(),
    })
change = pd.DataFrame(change)
change.round(2).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_member_profile.csv"), index=False)
print("\nMember profile by era:\n", change.round(2).to_string(index=False))

# Death causes among Everest deaths in the member table, by era
deaths_mem = mem[mem.died]
causes = pd.crosstab(deaths_mem.death_cause, deaths_mem.era)
causes.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "death_causes_by_era.csv"))
print("\nDeath causes by era (member table):\n", causes.to_string())

# Expedition structure by era
per_exp = exp.groupby("era").agg(
    expeditions=("expedition_id", "size"),
    mean_members=("members", "mean"),
    mean_hired=("hired_staff", "mean"),
    oxygen_expedition_share_pct=("oxygen_used", lambda s: 100 * s.mean()),
    agency_named_share_pct=("trekking_agency", lambda s: 100 * s.notna().mean()),
)
per_exp.round(2).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_expedition_profile.csv"))
print("\nExpedition profile by era:\n", per_exp.round(2).to_string())

# ---------- 5. charts ----------
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 11, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
C_MEM, C_HIRED, C_GREY = "#1f4e79", "#c0504d", "#7f7f7f"

# Chart 1: death rates by decade (1960s onward; 1950s has only 9 expeditions)
d = dec[dec.decade >= 1960].copy()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ax.plot(d.decade, d.hired_death_rate_pct, marker="o", color=C_HIRED, lw=2.2, label="Hired staff")
ax.plot(d.decade, d.member_death_rate_pct, marker="o", color=C_MEM, lw=2.2, label="Expedition members")
ax.axvline(COMMERCIAL_START, color=C_GREY, ls="--", lw=1)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(d.hired_death_rate_pct.max(), d.member_death_rate_pct.max()) * 1.3)
ax.text(COMMERCIAL_START + 1, 0.08, "Commercial era\nbegins (1990)", color=C_GREY, fontsize=10)
ax.set_xlabel("Decade of expedition")
ax.set_ylabel("Deaths per 100 people on expeditions")
ax.set_title("Everest death rates by decade: hired staff vs expedition members")
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right")
for x, h, m in zip(d.decade, d.hired_death_rate_pct, d.member_death_rate_pct):
    hi_above = h >= m
    ax.annotate(f"{h:.1f}", (x, h), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8 if hi_above else -16),
                ha="center", fontsize=9, color=C_HIRED)
    ax.annotate(f"{m:.1f}", (x, m), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, -16 if hi_above else 8),
                ha="center", fontsize=9, color=C_MEM)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(HERE, "chart1_death_rate_by_decade.png"), dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 2: era comparison with 95% CIs
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
labels = ["Pre-commercial\n(1921-1989)", "Commercial\n(1990-2019)"]
x = np.arange(2)
w = 0.35
for i, (who, col) in enumerate([("Expedition members", C_MEM), ("Hired staff", C_HIRED)]):
    sub = era[era.group == who].set_index("era").loc[[PRE, COM]]
    yerr = [sub.death_rate_pct - sub.ci_low_pct, sub.ci_high_pct - sub.death_rate_pct]
    ax.bar(x + (i - 0.5) * w, sub.death_rate_pct, w, color=col, label=who, yerr=yerr, capsize=4)
    for xi, v in zip(x + (i - 0.5) * w, sub.death_rate_pct):
        ax.text(xi, v + 0.25, f"{v:.1f}%", ha="center", fontsize=10)
ax.set_xticks(x, labels)
ax.set_ylabel("Deaths per 100 people (95% CI)")
ax.set_title("Death rate on Everest, before vs during the commercial era")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(HERE, "chart2_era_comparison.png"), dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 3: people on expeditions per decade
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
d2 = dec[dec.decade >= 1950]
ax.bar(d2.decade, d2.members, width=7, color=C_MEM, alpha=0.85, label="Expedition members")
ax.bar(d2.decade, d2.hired_staff, width=3, color=C_HIRED, alpha=0.9, label="Hired staff (above base camp)")
ax.set_xlabel("Decade of expedition")
ax.set_ylabel("People on Everest expeditions (total)")
ax.set_title("Everest: people on expeditions per decade")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(HERE, "chart3_people_by_decade.png"), dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Has climbing Everest become safer over time?

**Yes, for both expedition members and hired staff, measured per person.** The death rate roughly halved after 1990. Hired staff saw the bigger drop. The member rate has been flat at about 1 death per 100 climbers since 2000, so the gain is not still accelerating.

## Evidence

Source: Himalayan Database extract in `data/`, Everest only (`peak_id = EVER`), 2,149 expeditions, 1921–2019. Script: `analysis.py`. Full output: `run_log.txt`.

| Era | Expedition members: deaths / people (rate, 95% CI) | Hired staff: deaths / people (rate, 95% CI) |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-commercial, 1921–1989 | 58 / 2,961 = **2.0%** (1.5–2.5%) | 52 / 2,530 = **2.1%** (1.6–2.7%) |
| Commercial, 1990–2019 | 128 / 12,320 = **1.0%** (0.9–1.2%) | 68 / 10,211 = **0.7%** (0.5–0.8%) |

- Rate ratio, commercial vs pre-commercial: members 0.53 (chi-square p = 4e-5); hired staff 0.32 (p = 9e-11).

Decade rates (deaths per 100 people):

| Decade | 1960 | 1970 | 1980 | 1990 | 2000 | 2010 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Expedition members | 2.2 | 1.6 | 2.0 | 1.4 | 1.0 | 0.9 |
| Hired staff | 0.6 | 2.4 | 2.0 | 1.1 | 0.3 | 0.8 |

Hired-staff deaths are lumpy. 2014 (17 deaths) and 2015 (11) account for 28 of the 40 hired-staff deaths in the 2010s. Excluding those two years, the hired-staff rate for the 2010s is 0.28% (12 / 4,365), and the commercial-era rate is 0.42%. The member rate does not depend on those years: it is 1.10% without them.

Deaths per 100 summits (expedition members): 26.5 before 1990 vs 2.6 after. Part of this is denominator: the share of members who reached the summit rose from 7.8% to 39.9%.

## What changed in the commercial era

- **Who goes:** average expedition size fell from 14.5 members to 6.3. Hired staff per expedition fell from 12.4 to 5.3.
- **Equipment and support:** oxygen use among members rose from 20% to 53%. A named trekking agency appears on 97% of expeditions, up from 26%.
- **Causes of death (share of each era's deaths):** avalanche fell from 31% to 22%; icefall collapse from 11% to 1.5%; falls from 29% to 20%. Altitude sickness (AMS) rose from 5% to 15%, exhaustion from 2% to 12%, and non-AMS illness from 5% to 10%.

## Method

1. **Scope:** Everest only. Death counts and headcounts come from the expedition-level totals (`members`, `member_deaths`, `hired_staff`, `hired_staff_deaths`). These reconcile with the member-level records for the 1980s–2010s, so I used them as the complete count.
2. **Member-level records** were used only for roles, causes of death, oxygen, and summit detail.
3. **Commercial era** = 1990 onward, as requested.
4. **Confidence intervals** are Wilson 95% intervals. The tests are person-level chi-square tests, which ignore clustering within expeditions, so treat the p-values as indicative.

## Caveats

- **Association, not causation.** Guided, oxygen-supported, shorter expeditions changed at the same time as the death rates fell. The data cannot separate these from better forecasting, rescue, route fixing, or fewer people taking on high-risk attempts.
- **Who the rate describes changed.** Per-person rates compare different mixes of people across eras (more clients, fewer staff-heavy expeditions).
- **Early decades are thin.** Before 1960 there are fewer than 30 expeditions per decade, so the 1950s and earlier are excluded from the chart.
- **Hired-staff detail is incomplete at the member level** before the 2000s. Hired-staff rates use the expedition-level totals, which do include them.
- **Data ends in 2019.** The 2020s and the 2024 season are not covered.
- **Event names** (2014 Khumbu icefall, 2015 base-camp avalanche) are outside context; the data only shows the years.

## Files

- `analysis.py` — full pipeline (run with `python -I analysis.py` from this folder)
- `chart1_death_rate_by_decade.png`, `chart2_era_comparison.png`, `chart3_people_by_decade.png`
- `decade_death_rates.csv`, `era_death_rates.csv`, `era_tests.csv`, `sensitivity_excl_2014_2015.csv`, `top_years_hired_deaths.csv`, `era_member_profile.csv`, `death_causes_by_era.csv`, `era_expedition_profile.csv`

# Is Everest safer now? Yes, roughly half as deadly per person since 1990

Everest has become safer, and the gain is largest for the hired Sherpa and support staff who carry most of the load. But the improvement has leveled off, and a few disaster years still decide how bad any single season is.

![Death rates by decade](chart1_death_rate_by_decade.png)

## The short version

Between the pre-commercial era (1921–1989) and the commercial era (1990–2019):

- **Expedition members:** death rate fell from **2.0 to 1.0 per 100** people.
- **Hired staff:** death rate fell from **2.1 to 0.7 per 100** people.

![Before and after 1990](chart2_era_comparison.png)

## Where the gain came from

Staff risk fell fastest. In the 1970s and 1980s the hired-staff rate was about 2 per 100, around 2.4 in the 1970s. By the 2000s it had dropped to about 0.3 per 100 in the years without a disaster. Members improved more slowly: about 2.0 per 100 in the 1980s, 1.0 in the 2000s, and 0.9 in the 2010s.

## What changed on the mountain

The commercial era changed who climbs and how:

- **Smaller teams:** an average expedition went from 14.5 members to 6.3.
- **More oxygen:** the share of members using it rose from 20% to 53%.
- **More guided trips:** a named trekking agency appears on 97% of expeditions, up from 26%.
- **Different killers:** avalanches and icefall collapses made up a smaller share of deaths. Altitude sickness rose from 5% to 15% of deaths, and exhaustion from 2% to 12%.

## The catch: it has plateaued, and it is lumpy

Member death rates have stayed near 1 per 100 since 2000, so the trend has flattened. Hired-staff deaths are concentrated in a few years. The 2014 and 2015 seasons alone account for 28 of the 40 hired-staff deaths in the 2010s. Without those two years, the commercial-era staff rate falls to 0.4 per 100. Member rates barely move: 1.1 per 100 either way.

## What this does and does not show

This data shows that deaths per person have fallen, and that the mix of people and equipment changed at the same time. It does not prove that any one change caused the fall: better forecasting, rescue, and route work may all have contributed. The data also stops in 2019.

*Source: Himalayan Database extract for Everest (2,149 expeditions, 1921–2019). Full method and numbers in `answer.md`.*

# Has climbing Everest become safer over time?

**Yes, for both expedition members and hired staff, measured per person.** The death rate roughly halved after 1990. Hired staff saw the bigger drop. The member rate has been flat at about 1 death per 100 climbers since 2000, so the gain is not still accelerating.

## Evidence

Source: Himalayan Database extract in `data/`, Everest only (`peak_id = EVER`), 2,149 expeditions, 1921–2019. Script: `analysis.py`. Full output: `run_log.txt`.

| Era | Expedition members: deaths / people (rate, 95% CI) | Hired staff: deaths / people (rate, 95% CI) |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-commercial, 1921–1989 | 58 / 2,961 = **2.0%** (1.5–2.5%) | 52 / 2,530 = **2.1%** (1.6–2.7%) |
| Commercial, 1990–2019 | 128 / 12,320 = **1.0%** (0.9–1.2%) | 68 / 10,211 = **0.7%** (0.5–0.8%) |

- Rate ratio, commercial vs pre-commercial: members 0.53 (chi-square p = 4e-5); hired staff 0.32 (p = 9e-11).

Decade rates (deaths per 100 people):

| Decade | 1960 | 1970 | 1980 | 1990 | 2000 | 2010 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Expedition members | 2.2 | 1.6 | 2.0 | 1.4 | 1.0 | 0.9 |
| Hired staff | 0.6 | 2.4 | 2.0 | 1.1 | 0.3 | 0.8 |

Hired-staff deaths are lumpy. 2014 (17 deaths) and 2015 (11) account for 28 of the 40 hired-staff deaths in the 2010s. Excluding those two years, the hired-staff rate for the 2010s is 0.27% (12 / 4,365), and the commercial-era rate is 0.42%. The member rate does not depend on those years: it is 1.10% without them.

Deaths per 100 summits (expedition members): 26.5 before 1990 vs 2.6 after. Part of this is denominator: the share of members who reached the summit rose from 7.8% to 39.9%.

- **Who goes:** average expedition size fell from 14.5 members to 6.3. Hired staff per expedition fell from 12.4 to 5.3.

2. **Member-level records** were used only for roles, causes of death, oxygen, and summit detail.
3. **Commercial era** = 1990 onward, as requested.
4. **Confidence intervals** are Wilson 95% intervals. The tests are person-level chi-square tests, which ignore clustering within expeditions, so treat the p-values as indicative.

- **Event names** (2014 Khumbu icefall, 2015 base-camp avalanche) are outside context; the data only shows the years.

| Era | Members: deaths per 100 (95% CI) | Hired staff: deaths per 100 (95% CI) |

"""Has climbing Mount Everest become safer over time?

Death rates for expedition members vs hired staff, by decade, and the
pre-commercial (1921-1989) vs commercial (1990-2019) comparison.

Run:  python -I analysis.py   (from this folder; reads ../../data, read-only)
"""
import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "data")
COMMERCIAL_START = 1990

# ---------- load ----------
exp_all = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, "expeditions.csv"))
mem_all = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, "members.csv"), low_memory=False)
exp = exp_all[exp_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()
mem = mem_all[mem_all.peak_id == "EVER"].copy()
print(f"Everest expeditions: {len(exp)} ({exp.year.min()}-{exp.year.max()})")
print(f"Everest member rows: {len(mem)}")

# Expedition-level totals are the complete record of people and deaths.
# Member-level rows are used for roles, causes and summit detail.
exp["era"] = np.where(exp.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, "Commercial (1990-2019)", "Pre-commercial (1921-1989)")
mem["era"] = np.where(mem.year >= COMMERCIAL_START, "Commercial (1990-2019)", "Pre-commercial (1921-1989)")
exp["decade"] = (exp.year // 10) * 10
mem["decade"] = (mem.year // 10) * 10


def wilson(k, n, z=1.96):
    """Wilson 95% CI for a proportion k/n."""
    if n == 0:
        return (np.nan, np.nan)
    p = k / n
    denom = 1 + z**2 / n
    centre = (p + z**2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = z * np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z**2 / (4 * n**2)) / denom
    return (centre - half, centre + half)


# ---------- 1. decade table (expedition-level totals) ----------
g = exp.groupby("decade")
dec = pd.DataFrame({
    "expeditions": g.size(),
    "members": g.members.sum(),
    "member_deaths": g.member_deaths.sum(),
    "hired_staff": g.hired_staff.sum(),
    "hired_staff_deaths": g.hired_staff_deaths.sum(),
})
dec["member_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.member_deaths / dec.members
dec["hired_death_rate_pct"] = 100 * dec.hired_staff_deaths / dec.hired_staff
dec["hired_per_member"] = dec.hired_staff / dec.members
dec["small_sample_flag"] = (dec.members < 100) | (dec.hired_staff < 100)
dec = dec.reset_index()
dec.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "decade_death_rates.csv"), index=False)
print("\nDecade table:\n", dec.round(2).to_string(index=False))

# ---------- 2. era comparison with CIs and tests ----------
era_rows = []
for era, sub in exp.groupby("era"):
    for who, k_col, n_col in [("Expedition members", "member_deaths", "members"),
                              ("Hired staff", "hired_staff_deaths", "hired_staff")]:
        k, n = int(sub[k_col].sum()), int(sub[n_col].sum())
        lo, hi = wilson(k, n)
        era_rows.append({"era": era, "group": who, "deaths": k, "people": n,
                         "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n, "ci_low_pct": 100 * lo, "ci_high_pct": 100 * hi})
era = pd.DataFrame(era_rows)
era.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_death_rates.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra table:\n", era.round(3).to_string(index=False))

tests = []
pre = exp[exp.era.str.startswith("Pre")]
com = exp[exp.era.str.startswith("Com")]
for who, k_col, n_col in [("Expedition members", "member_deaths", "members"),
                          ("Hired staff", "hired_staff_deaths", "hired_staff")]:
    table = np.array([
        [pre[k_col].sum(), pre[n_col].sum() - pre[k_col].sum()],
        [com[k_col].sum(), com[n_col].sum() - com[k_col].sum()],
    ])
    chi2, p, _, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(table, correction=False)
    rr = (com[k_col].sum() / com[n_col].sum()) / (pre[k_col].sum() / pre[n_col].sum())
    tests.append({"group": who, "rate_ratio_commercial_vs_pre": rr, "chi2": chi2, "p_value": p})
tests = pd.DataFrame(tests)
tests.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_tests.csv"), index=False)
print("\nEra tests (person-level chi-square; ignores expedition clustering):\n", tests.to_string(index=False))

# ---------- 3. sensitivity: commercial era without the two icefall/avalanche disasters ----------
# 2014 (Khumbu icefall, 16 Sherpa killed) and 2015 (base camp avalanche, 19 killed)
sens_rows = []
for label, sub in [("Commercial, all years", com),
                   ("Commercial, excl. 2014-2015", com[~com.year.isin([2014, 2015])])]:
    k, n = int(sub.hired_staff_deaths.sum()), int(sub.hired_staff.sum())
    sens_rows.append({"sample": label, "group": "Hired staff", "deaths": k, "people": n, "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n})
    k, n = int(sub.member_deaths.sum()), int(sub.members.sum())
    sens_rows.append({"sample": label, "group": "Expedition members", "deaths": k, "people": n, "death_rate_pct": 100 * k / n})
sens = pd.DataFrame(sens_rows)
sens.round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "sensitivity_excl_2014_2015.csv"), index=False)
print("\nSensitivity:\n", sens.round(3).to_string(index=False))

# Single-year spikes in hired-staff deaths
yr = exp.groupby("year").agg(hired_staff_deaths=("hired_staff_deaths", "sum"),
                             member_deaths=("member_deaths", "sum"),
                             hired_staff=("hired_staff", "sum"),
                             members=("members", "sum"))
top_years = yr.sort_values("hired_staff_deaths", ascending=False).head(8)
top_years.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "top_years_hired_deaths.csv"))
print("\nTop years by hired-staff deaths:\n", top_years.to_string())

# ---------- 4. commercial-era changes (member-level detail) ----------
mem_m = mem[~mem.hired]  # expedition members (not hired)
mem_m = mem_m.assign(summit=mem_m.success.astype(bool))
change = []
for era_name, sub in mem_m.groupby("era"):
    n = len(sub)
    change.append({
        "era": era_name,
        "member_rows": n,
        "oxygen_share_pct": 100 * sub.oxygen_used.mean(),
        "summit_share_pct": 100 * sub.summit.mean(),
        "deaths_per_100_summits": 100 * sub.died.sum() / max(sub.summit.sum(), 1),
        "median_age": sub.age.median(),
        "female_share_pct": 100 * (sub.sex == "F").mean(),
    })
change = pd.DataFrame(change)
change.round(2).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_member_profile.csv"), index=False)
print("\nMember profile by era:\n", change.round(2).to_string(index=False))

# Death causes among all Everest deaths in member table, by era
deaths_mem = mem[mem.died]
causes = pd.crosstab(deaths_mem.death_cause, deaths_mem.era)
causes.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "death_causes_by_era.csv"))
print("\nDeath causes by era (member table):\n", causes.to_string())

# Hired staff per expedition-member (commercial structure)
per_exp = exp.groupby("era").agg(
    expeditions=("expedition_id", "size"),
    mean_members=("members", "mean"),
    mean_hired=("hired_staff", "mean"),
    oxygen_expedition_share_pct=("oxygen_used", lambda s: 100 * s.mean()),
    agency_named_share_pct=("trekking_agency", lambda s: 100 * s.notna().mean()),
)
per_exp.round(2).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "era_expedition_profile.csv"))
print("\nExpedition profile by era:\n", per_exp.round(2).to_string())

# ---------- 5. charts ----------
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 11, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
C_MEM, C_HIRED, C_GREY = "#1f4e79", "#c0504d", "#7f7f7f"

# Chart 1: death rates by decade
d = dec[dec.decade >= 1950].copy()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ax.plot(d.decade, d.hired_death_rate_pct, marker="o", color=C_HIRED, lw=2.2, label="Hired staff")
ax.plot(d.decade, d.member_death_rate_pct, marker="o", color=C_MEM, lw=2.2, label="Expedition members")
ax.axvline(COMMERCIAL_START, color=C_GREY, ls="--", lw=1)
ax.text(COMMERCIAL_START + 1, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.93, "Commercial era begins (1990)", color=C_GREY, fontsize=10)
ax.set_xlabel("Decade of expedition")
ax.set_ylabel("Deaths per 100 people on expeditions")
ax.set_title("Everest death rates by decade: hired staff vs expedition members")
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right")
for x, y in zip(d.decade, d.hired_death_rate_pct):
    if np.isfinite(y):
        ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 7), ha="center", fontsize=9, color=C_HIRED)
for x, y in zip(d.decade, d.member_death_rate_pct):
    if np.isfinite(y):
        ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, -15), ha="center", fontsize=9, color=C_MEM)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(HERE, "chart1_death_rate_by_decade.png"), dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 2: era comparison with 95% CIs
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
labels = ["Pre-commercial\n(1921-1989)", "Commercial\n(1990-2019)"]
x = np.arange(2)
w = 0.35
for i, (who, col) in enumerate([("Expedition members", C_MEM), ("Hired staff", C_HIRED)]):
    sub = era[era.group == who].set_index("era").loc[
        ["Pre-commercial (1921-1989)", "Commercial (1990-2019)"]]
    yerr = [sub.death_rate_pct - sub.ci_low_pct, sub.ci_high_pct - sub.death_rate_pct]
    bars = ax.bar(x + (i - 0.5) * w, sub.death_rate_pct, w, color=col, label=who, yerr=yerr, capsize=4)
    for xi, v in zip(x + (i - 0.5) * w, sub.death_rate_pct):
        ax.text(xi, v + 0.25, f"{v:.1f}%", ha="center", fontsize=10)
ax.set_xticks(x, labels)
ax.set_ylabel("Deaths per 100 people (95% CI)")
ax.set_title("Death rate on Everest, before vs during the commercial era")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(HERE, "chart2_era_comparison.png"), dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 3: who goes and how many staff per climber
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
d2 = dec[dec.decade >= 1950]
ax.bar(d2.decade, d2.members, width=7, color=C_MEM, alpha=0.85, label="Expedition members")
ax.bar(d2.decade, d2.hired_staff, width=3, color=C_HIRED, alpha=0.9, label="Hired staff (above base camp)")
ax.set_xlabel("Decade of expedition")
ax.set_ylabel("People on Everest expeditions (total)")
ax.set_title("Everest: people on expeditions per decade")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(HERE, "chart3_people_by_decade.png"), dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

print("\nDone. Outputs written to", HERE)
